To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have synthesized rhombohedral-shaped hematite nanocrystals with rounded edges and have studied their morphology and microstructure as a function of the aging time, and that we have investigated the vibrational and electronic properties of such nanocrystalline samples.

the vibrational bands of rhombohederal-shaped hematite nanocrystals are shifted to lower frequencies as the size is reduced due to phonons confinement effects and the indirect and direct band gaps displayed interesting dependence on the aging time, which arise from quantum confinement and the surface effects.

the morphology of rhombohederal-shape α-Fe2O₃ nanocrystals is controlled by the aging time of the hydrolysis solution and the nanocrystals are characterized by a high surface-to-volume ratio and a large number of pores and fissures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of novel nanocrystalline materials for applications in catalysis and photocatalysis.
the synthesis, microstructural and optical characterization of hematite (Fe2O3), a magnetic material with great potential for technological applications.
the synthesis and characterization of hematite (alpha-Fe2O(3)) nanocrystals with rhombohedral shapes and rounded edges.

the nanocrystalline hematite (α - Fe2O3) is a promising candidate to be used in a variety of applications such as photocatalysis, magnetic and electronic devices, sensors, and so on.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nanocrystal formation mechanism is a combination of a fast nucleation followed by slow crystal growth, the crystal growth is mainly controlled by the diffusion of iron(III)-containing ions and the crystal growth rate depends on the concentration and pH of the iron(III) solution.
the morphology of hematite nanocrystals can be controlled by the aging time of the reaction.
the confinement and surface effects on vibrational and optical properties of rhomboedral hematite (α -Fe2O3 )nanocrystals are studied as a function of the aging time and size of the nanocrystal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vibrational properties of rhombohedrally shaped hematite nanocrystals can be tailored by controlling the nanocrystal morphology, size and surface state.
the confinement effect is not only related to the nanocrystal sizes but it is also related to the shape and the morphology of nanocrystals.

the physical properties of nanocrystals with rhombohedral morphology are strongly influenced by confinement effects and surface effects, which should be taken into account when designing new applications for these nanocrystals.
